# Virtual file systems

The commands `mt help` lists under Virtual file systems. File systems are known as virtual file systems (VFS) in Maitento, which is why these commands start with `vfs-`. More in [File systems](../../../concepts/file-systems.md).

In a terminal, type `mt` and then the command. In the interactive shell and the cloud shell, type the command on
its own. `mt help <command>` shows the same details in your terminal.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`vfs-create`](#vfs-create) | Create an empty file system in a namespace |
| [`vfs-destroy`](#vfs-destroy) | Delete a file system and every file in it (there is no confirmation) |
| [`vfs-get`](#vfs-get) | Show a file system by name: its id, status and where it is mounted |
| [`vfs-list`](#vfs-list) | List the file systems in a namespace |
| [`vfs-sync`](#vfs-sync) | Mirror a directory on your disk into a file system, creating it if needed (adds, overwrites and deletes to match) *(not in the cloud shell)* |

## vfs-create

Create an empty file system in a namespace.

```text
mt vfs-create <name> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<name>` | text | yes |  | Name of the file system, unique in the namespace |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |

## vfs-destroy

Delete a file system and every file in it (there is no confirmation).

```text
mt vfs-destroy <name> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<name>` | text | yes |  | Name of the file system |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |

## vfs-get

Show a file system by name: its id, status and where it is mounted.

```text
mt vfs-get <name> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<name>` | text | yes |  | Name of the file system |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |

## vfs-list

List the file systems in a namespace.

```text
mt vfs-list [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |

## vfs-sync

Mirror a directory on your disk into a file system, creating it if needed (adds, overwrites and deletes to match).

```text
mt vfs-sync <source> <name> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<source>` | text | yes |  | The directory on your disk to copy from |
| `<name>` | text | yes |  | Name of the file system to mirror into |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--exclude <value>` | text |  |  | Directory names to leave out wherever they appear, comma-separated (e.g. bin,obj,node_modules) |
| `--allow-empty` | flag |  |  | Allow a source with no files, which empties the file system (refused without this) |

**Not available in the cloud shell:** it mirrors a directory from the local disk, and the cloud shell has none.
